title: A Day Trip Around Western Incheon: Celadon, a K-Drama Lake Park, and an Easy Mountain Trail
html:
If you've got a free day around Incheon and want to see more than just the airport, here's a beginner-friendly day-trip course in western Incheon that mixes history, a famous K-drama photo spot, and an easy mountain walk. It links three free, low-key places — the Nokcheongja Museum, Cheongna Lake Park, and the Gyeyangsan Mountain Trail — that aren't crowded with tourists, so it's a nice slower-paced day if you already have extra time around Incheon rather than rushing straight to Seoul.

Stop 1 (Morning): Nokcheongja Museum

Start the day at the Nokcheongja Museum (녹청자박물관), a small, free museum built right next to the real kiln site where potters fired cheongja (celadon, the jade-green Korean pottery you've probably seen in other museums) more than a thousand years ago. "Nokcheongja" refers to an early, greenish style of celadon that was made on this exact spot, before the more famous jade-green Goryeo celadon came later.

Inside, two small halls walk you through how celadon was actually made (shaping, glazing, firing) and show modern Korean ceramic artists using the same techniques today. There's also an outdoor area with around 200 donated pottery pieces worth a short walk-through.

  • Address: 54 Doyoji-ro, Seo-gu, Incheon
  • Hours: 09:00–18:00 (last admission 17:30), closed Mondays
  • Admission: Free

This museum sits in a quiet residential part of western Incheon with no single well-known subway station nearby. The easiest way in is to type the museum's name into Naver Map or Kakao Map — these are the apps Korean locals actually use to get around, and they're usually more accurate than Google Maps inside Korea — and take a taxi or bus from wherever you're starting. Plan for about an hour here, including the outdoor area.

Stop 2 (Midday): Cheongna Lake Park

From the museum, head about 15–20 minutes by taxi or bus to Cheongna Lake Park, a waterfront park in the middle of Cheongna International City with three small islands and a 4-kilometer circular walking path. It's a relaxed spot for lunch and a walk, with a musical fountain, a rose garden, and water leisure activities in warmer months.

Fans of Korean dramas may recognize this park: the city built a baduk (Korean board game, similar to Go) board plaza here to recreate a set from the Netflix series The Glory. As of late 2024, the spot had an interactive photo booth where you sit at the baduk board and turn your photo into an animated version of a character from the show — fun even if you haven't seen the drama. Note that these pop-up photo zones can change or close over time, so it's worth checking it's still running before making a special trip just for that.

  • Address: 59 Crystal-ro, Seo-gu, Incheon
  • Hours: Open 24 hours, year-round
  • Admission & parking: Both free
  • Getting there: About a 15-minute walk from Cheongna International City Station on the Incheon Airport Railroad (AREX) line

There are casual restaurants and cafés in the Cheongna Central Plaza area right next to the park, so this is the easiest spot on the route to grab lunch.

Stop 3 (Afternoon): Gyeyangsan Mountain Trail

To finish the day, take a taxi or bus about 20–25 minutes east to the Gyeyangsan Mountain Trail (계양산둘레길), a loop path around the base of 395-meter Gyeyangsan Mountain. The full loop is about 7.3 kilometers and takes roughly 2 hours, with a decked walkway for most of the route — easier underfoot than a typical dirt hiking trail, and fine for most fitness levels since you're walking around the mountain rather than up it.

If you're short on time or energy after the first two stops, it's completely fine to just walk part of the loop near the start and turn back — there's no single "must-see" viewpoint you'd be missing, and it's really about the easy forest walk itself.

  • Starting point: Gyeyangsan Outdoor Theater, Danam-dong, Gyeyang-gu, Incheon
  • Admission & parking: Both free
  • Getting there: About a 5-minute walk from exits 5–6 of Gyesan Station on Incheon Subway Line 1

This is also the most convenient stop to end on, since Incheon Subway Line 1 connects onward into the Seoul subway network — handy if you're heading back into the city afterward.
